newsitem.title: USA: Republican leads Democrat for Colorado Senate.
newsitem.headline: Republican leads Democrat for Colorado Senate.

text.p: The Republican candidate for the open U.S. Senate seat in Colorado has edged ahead of his Democratic rival in a hotly contested and closely watched race, according to a poll published on Friday.

Wayne Allard, who currently represents Colorado's fourth congressional district, led lawyer Tom Strickland by 48 percent to 42 percent, according to a poll conducted by the Rocky Mountain News and local television station KMGH.
The poll of 600 likely voters has a margin of error of four percentage points.
The two are vying for the seat that Republican Hank Brown is vacating after one term.
Environmental issues and Strickland's role as a lobbyist have become major issues in the race.
Ten percent of those surveyed favored other candidates or did not know how they would vote.
In a previous poll Strickland was ahead of Allard by 46 percent to 39 percent with 15 percent undecided.
